language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, my name is Tim. Welcome to Scotland!
Hi, my name is Montgomery. My family owns a kilt shop in Scotland where we live. Our kilts are made of wool, which is a natural fiber.

Wool is the fur of sheep. Each year, we shave it off and use it to make clothes. It takes only one year for the wool to regrow. So, as long as sheep get grass to eat, they will keep producing wool. This makes wool a renewable resource.

In contrast, synthetic fibers such as polyester or nylon, require oil for production. Oil is a non-renewable resource. Come, let's explore more about the types of natural resources and discover why they are so important to us.

Our planet provides many natural resources of energy. It takes the earth millions of years to produce fossil fuels, like oils and gas. We call these non-renewable resources
of energy.

We installed solar panels on the roof to generate renewable electricity for
our store.
The solar panels will help us reduce the use of fossil fuels to create electricity.
Do you know other natural resources used for energy?
As part of my school assignment, I'm making a chart of natural resources of energy. I could really use your help!
